title: Raymond Scott and his brother Mark Warnow on the Hit Parade
summary: Leeman is offered a job on the Hit Parade after Raymond Scott took over his late brother Mark's conducting post, and Hinton praises their role in popular music.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Most grateful. So I worked with him, and about that year -- '51, I was approached, Raymond Scott, his brother had died and he acquired his brother's job on the Hit Parade.
Let's just mention a little of this before I go. Raymond Scott's brother was who?
Mark Warner was the leader on the Hit Parade over the years, and he was the conductor when Frank was around, becoming a bigger name as a single.
For some particular reason, they took different names.
Well, I guess it's better, yeah. Like you say, we used to call Raymond Scott --
But you never called him Mark, did you, or you never called him Warner.
Oh, no, his name wasn't Mark. Mark Warner I never worked for -- but he had the job, anyway; we used to call Raymond Scott, his tuxedo in his brother's orchestra. But that's just a bit of trivia.

Well, it's nice to mention that because down through the years, these two gentlemen did so much for music, especially popular music, American popular music, and there hasn't been enough written about American popular
music which is Americana, I believe, as much as jazz in some respects. And I think that Mark Warner and radio and television and also, Raymond Scott --
